title: Lehet + Infinitive – What's Possible or Allowed

sections.title: From "maybe" to "one is allowed to"
sections.content: You already know lehet on its own, meaning "maybe, it's possible." Add an infinitive and it takes on a new job: saying what's generally possible or allowed, for anyone — Itt lehet parkolni ("You can park here" / "Parking is allowed here"). Like kell and kellene, lehet never changes for person; it just states that something is or isn't an option.

items.spanish: Itt lehet enni gyümölcsöt és zöldséget.
items.english: You can eat fruit and vegetables here.
You're not allowed to smoke in the hospital.

items.spanish: Este már nem lehet sportolni a parkban.
items.english: In the evening you can no longer exercise in the park.

sections.content: lehet describes what the situation or the rules allow, tud describes what a person is personally capable of — Nem lehet itt aludni ("sleeping here isn't allowed") is about the place, while Nem tudok aludni ("I can't sleep") is about you.
